dimensions.label: Cheapest way to get a live, sellable store
dimensions.a: $39/mo (Basic) — hosting, checkout and unlimited products included, 0% extra fee via Shopify Payments
dimensions.b: $42/mo (Ecommerce Standard) — capped at 500 items, plus a 2% fee on top of Stripe or PayPal

dimensions.label: Transaction fee on top of card processing
dimensions.a: 0% with Shopify Payments on Basic; a different processor costs 2% (Basic), 1% (Grow) or 0.6% (Advanced)
dimensions.b: 2% on every sale on Ecommerce Standard, no matter the processor; $84/mo Ecommerce Plus removes it

dimensions.label: Ecommerce catalog size before you must upgrade
dimensions.a: Unlimited products on every paid plan, from Basic up

dimensions.label: Selling in person with a point-of-sale system
dimensions.a: Built into every paid plan; POS Pro adds advanced tools at $89 per location a month
dimensions.b: No point-of-sale system, built in or as an add-on

dimensions.label: How team members are billed
dimensions.a: Bundled into the plan: 0 staff (Basic), 5 (Grow, $105/mo), 15 (Advanced, $399/mo) — no per-seat fee
dimensions.b: Billed per person on top of the Site plan: $45/mo for a Full seat, $19/mo for a Limited seat

dimensions.label: What drives the bill up as traffic grows
dimensions.a: Nothing — the plan price does not change with visits or bandwidth
dimensions.b: Bandwidth: 50 GB/mo included on Premium, then paid tiers up to $560/mo for 1 TB

dimensions.label: Content beyond the store: blog and marketing pages
dimensions.a: A basic blog exists, but Shopify's CMS is not built for large content-marketing sites
dimensions.b: Premium's CMS handles 20,000 items across 40 Collections — built for this

dimensions.label: Design and layout control over the storefront
dimensions.a: Shopify's themes, apps and Liquid templating language set the boundaries
dimensions.b: A full visual canvas plus custom code, and code components on Premium

dimensions.label: Free plan you can actually build something on
dimensions.a: Agentic ($0) lists products in Shopify's own channels but can't publish a store or take checkout orders
dimensions.b: Starter ($0) builds and tests without limit, but only on a webflow.io subdomain, capped at 2 pages and 50 CMS items

dimensions.label: Moving to a different platform later
dimensions.a: Not possible without a full rebuild — a Shopify store only runs on Shopify's own servers
dimensions.b: Partial — paid Workspace plans export HTML/CSS, but cart, checkout and CMS content don't come with it

dimensions.label: Billing commitment at the top tier
dimensions.a: Plus starts at $2,500/mo on a required 1-year term, no month-to-month option
dimensions.b: Team starts at $2,500/mo on a required annual contract, no month-to-month option

verdicts.why: A catalog business needs Shopify's unlimited products, built-in point-of-sale and a 0% fee with Shopify Payments; only pick Webflow instead if the catalog stays under 500 items and the site's design and content matter as much as the checkout.

An agency building client marketing sites gets more value from Webflow's visual design control and CMS than from a checkout, and reaches for Shopify only when a client's site is specifically a product-catalog store.
A course or coaching business runs on cohort, drip-content and community tools that neither platform provides; both are built to ship a product catalog or a marketing site, not a curriculum.
A booking-and-invoice business needs scheduling software first; add Shopify or Webflow only once it also sells a real product line alongside the services.
A freelancer's site is usually a portfolio and a client pipeline, which is a design and content job that fits Webflow, not a storefront built for inventory.
A software company's marketing site is a design, CMS and page-speed job that Webflow fits directly; Shopify has no reason to be in a software business's stack.
